items.title: Section: The Third Characteristic Opens — Eight Kinds of Reliance, Beginning With the Five Aggregates of Clinging

items.zh: 一、施設依，二、攝受依，三、住持依，四、流轉依，五、障礙依，六、苦惱依，七、適悅依，八、後邊依。云何施設依？謂五取蘊。由依此故，施設我及有情、命者、生者、能養育者、補特伽羅、意生、儒童等，諸想等想假用言說。及依此故，施設如是名字、如是生類、如是種姓、如是飲食、如是領受苦樂、如是長壽、如是久住、如是壽量邊際等，諸想等想假用言說。
items.en:
Fourth, explaining; first, the reliance of designation; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of designation?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. The five aggregates of clinging.
Second, clarifying designation; first, the notion of a person. In reliance on this, one designates self, being, life-holder, one who arises, nurturer, one who repeatedly takes rebirth, mind-born one, youthful one, and so forth — every such notion, in all its varieties, being a provisional label adopted for speech.
Second, the notion of the eight sayings. And in reliance on this, one designates such a name, such a kind of birth, such a lineage, such food, such experience of pleasure and pain, such a long lifespan, such a duration of dwelling, and such the very limit of one's lifespan, and so forth — every such notion, in all its varieties, being a provisional label adopted for speech.

items.title: Section: Seven People Who Care for Us, and Four Kinds of Food That Keep a Being Alive

items.zh: 云何攝受依？謂七攝受事。即自己父母、妻子、奴婢、作使、僮僕、朋友、眷屬，七攝受事。如前意地已廣分別。依此了知諸有情類有所攝受。云何住持依？謂四種食。即段食、觸食、意思食、識食。由依此故，已生有情住立支持；又能攝養諸求有者。
items.en:
Second, the reliance of being cared for; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of being cared for?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. Seven matters of being cared for: one's own parents, spouse and children, servants and those directed, and friends and relatives — seven matters of being cared for, already explained at length in the Mind Ground.
Second, clarifying being cared for. In reliance on this, one understands that every kind of being has those who care for them.
Third, the reliance of sustenance; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of sustenance?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. Four kinds of food: edible food, contact food, volitional food, and consciousness food.
Second, clarifying sustenance. In reliance on this, a being already born is sustained and supported; and it also nourishes those seeking further existence to come.

items.title: Section: Four Stations Where Consciousness Takes Root, and the Twelve Links That Keep Rebirth Turning

items.zh: 云何流轉依？謂四種識住及十二緣起。即色趣識住、受趣識住、想趣識住、行趣識住；及無明緣行、行緣識，廣說乃至生緣老死。由依此故，諸有情類，於五趣生死隨順流轉。
items.en:
Fourth, the reliance of continued rebirth; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of continued rebirth?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. The four stations of consciousness and the twelve links of dependent origination: form as a station for consciousness, feeling as a station for consciousness, perception as a station for consciousness, mental formations as a station for consciousness; and ignorance conditions formations, formations condition consciousness, and so on at length through birth conditioning ageing and death.
Second, clarifying continued rebirth. In reliance on this, all kinds of beings continue turning through birth and death across the five destinies.

items.title: Section: Demons, Desire's Own Suffering, Meditative Ease, and the Final Body — the Eight Kinds of Reliance Complete

items.zh: 云何障礙依？謂諸天魔。隨有彼彼修善法處，即往其前，為作障礙。云何苦惱依？謂一切欲界皆名苦惱依。由依此故，令諸有情領受憂苦。云何適悅依？謂靜慮、等至樂名適悅依。由依此故，諸有情類若即於此現入彼定，若生於彼，長夜領受靜慮、等至所有適悅。云何後邊依？謂阿羅漢相續諸蘊。由依此故，說諸阿羅漢任持最後身。
items.en:
Fifth, the reliance of obstruction; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of obstruction?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. The heavenly demons.
Second, clarifying obstruction. Wherever wholesome dharma is being cultivated, they go before it and create obstruction.
Sixth, the reliance of suffering; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of suffering?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. The entire desire realm is called the reliance of suffering.
Second, clarifying suffering. In reliance on this, all beings experience sorrow and suffering.
Seventh, the reliance of pleasant ease; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of pleasant ease?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. The pleasure of meditative absorption and attainment is called the reliance of pleasant ease.
Second, clarifying pleasant ease. In reliance on this, beings who presently enter such attainment, or who are reborn there, experience this pleasant ease of absorption and attainment throughout the long night of saṃsāra.
Eighth, the reliance of the final limit; first, posing the question. What is the reliance of the final limit?
Second, explaining; first, presenting what is relied upon. An arhat's own continuing aggregates.
Second, clarifying the final limit. In reliance on this, arhats are said to abide in their very last body.

items.title: Section: Which Reliances Remain for a Liberated Arhat — and the Seventeenth, Final Stage Opens

items.zh: 問：阿羅漢苾芻諸漏永盡，住有餘依地，當言與幾種依共相應耶？答：當言與一種依一向相應，謂後邊依；與六攝受事不共相應；與流轉依、與障礙依，一向全不相應；與所餘依，非相應非不相應。是名依施設安立。如是已說有餘依地。云何無餘依地？
items.en:
Fifth, a further examination; first, posing the question. Question: an arhat monk, every outflow permanently exhausted, abiding in the Stage With Residue Remaining — with how many kinds of reliance should he be said to correspond?
Second, answering. Answer: he should be said to correspond fully and exclusively to one kind of reliance, namely the reliance of the final limit; he does not correspond to six matters of being cared for; he does not correspond at all to the reliance of continued rebirth or the reliance of obstruction; with the remaining reliances, he neither corresponds nor fails to correspond.
Sixth, concluding. This is called the establishment of reliance.
Within the basic section, the Stage With No Residue Remaining, the seventeenth.
Fourteenth, the Stage With No Residue Remaining; first, concluding what precedes and generating what follows. Thus the Stage With Residue Remaining has been explained. What is the Stage With No Residue Remaining?
Bodhisattva Jinaputra's own commentary explains: the Stage With No Residue Remaining is the ground of nirvāṇa without residue remaining. Every contaminated residue of reliance is relinquished; even the conditioned, uncontaminated qualities of the two lesser vehicles are also relinquished. Though the Tathāgata possesses conditioned, uncontaminated qualities, he is without any contaminated residue of reliance whatsoever; for this reason his attainment, too, is called the Stage With No Residue Remaining.

items.title: Section: Three Characteristics of the Final Stage, and Two Kinds of Ultimate Cessation

items.zh: 當知此地亦有三相。一者、地施設安立，二者、寂滅施設安立，三者、寂滅異門安立。云何地施設安立？謂先所除五地一分，當知即此無餘依地所攝。謂無心地、修所成地、聲聞地、獨覺地、菩薩地。云何寂滅施設安立？謂由二種寂滅，施設安立如是無餘依地。一、由寂靜寂滅故；二、由無損惱寂滅故。
items.en:
Second, correctly distinguishing the stage's characteristics; first, stating. Know that this stage, too, has three characteristics.
Second, listing them. First, the establishment of the stage; second, the establishment of cessation; third, the establishment of synonyms for cessation.
Third, explaining; first, the establishment of the stage; first, posing the question. What is the establishment of the stage?
Second, explaining. The portion previously excluded from the five stages — the stage without mind, the stage brought about by cultivation, the Śrāvaka Stage, the Pratyekabuddha Stage, and the Bodhisattva Stage — should be known as encompassed by this Stage With No Residue Remaining.
Second, the establishment of cessation; first, posing the question. What is the establishment of cessation?
Second, stating. This Stage With No Residue Remaining is established through two kinds of cessation.
Third, listing them. First, cessation through tranquility; second, cessation through freedom from affliction.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Ultimate Tranquility — Beyond All Reckoning, Like a Lamp Going Out

items.zh: 云何寂靜寂滅？謂先於有餘依地，獲得觸證四種寂靜；今無餘依涅槃界中，亦有最勝四種寂靜。一、數教寂靜，二、一切依寂靜，三、依依苦寂靜，四、依依苦生疑慮寂靜。如說：由無下劣心，能忍受勤苦，彼所趣解脫，譬如燈盡滅。云何無損惱寂滅？謂與一切依不相應，違背
items.en:
Fourth, explaining; first, cessation through tranquility; first, posing the question. What is cessation through tranquility?
Second, stating. Just as, in the Stage With Residue Remaining, one had already realised and personally verified four kinds of tranquility, so too, now within the realm of nirvāṇa without residue remaining, there are also four most excellent kinds of tranquility.
Third, listing them. First, tranquility beyond all reckoning; second, tranquility of every reliance; third, tranquility of the reliance and its suffering; fourth, tranquility from every doubt arising from the reliance's own suffering.
Commentary: as for tranquility beyond all reckoning — this means it cannot be reckoned through discrimination, and no verbal teaching whatsoever can describe it.
Commentary: as for tranquility of every reliance — the eight kinds of reliance are called "every reliance." Within the Stage With Residue Remaining, one might correspond or not correspond to them. Now, none of them correspond at all; hence it is called tranquility.
Commentary: as for tranquility of the reliance and its suffering — within the Stage With Residue Remaining, because a physical basis still remained, one was not entirely without correspondence to the reliance of suffering. Now this is not so; hence it is called tranquility of the reliance and its suffering.
Commentary: as for tranquility from doubt arising from the reliance's own suffering — "reliance" means the physical basis; suffering arising from that basis is called "the reliance's suffering." These two tranquilities carry the same meaning as explained before. In this very life, that resultant mental suffering never manifests at all.
Fourth, citing scriptural proof. As it is said: free of any inferior mind, capable of enduring diligent hardship, the liberation such a one attains is like a lamp going entirely out.
Commentary: as for this citation — this verse is cited specifically for its final two lines, proving cessation through tranquility, as should be understood.

items.title: Section: "There Is the Unborn, the Unmade" — Freedom From Affliction Proven Through the Reality of Liberation Itself

items.zh: 一切煩惱諸苦流轉，生起轉依所顯真無漏界。如說：苾芻永寂滅，名真安樂住。又如說言：實有無生、無起、無作、無為、無等生起；亦有有生、有起、有作、有為、有等生起。若當無有無生、無起、無作、無為、無等生起；我終不說有生、有起、有作、有為、有等生起、有永出離。由實有無生、無起、無作、無為、無等生起；是故我說有生、有起、有作、有為、有等生起、有永出離。
items.en:
Second, citing scriptural proof; first, proving freedom from suffering. As it is said: "a monk permanently pacified is called one truly dwelling in ease."
Second, proving the transformation of basis. And as it is also said: there truly is the unborn, the unarisen, the unmade, the unconditioned, and the unequal-arising; and there is also the born, the arisen, the made, the conditioned, and the equal-arising.
Were there no such thing as the unborn, the unarisen, the unmade, the unconditioned, and the unequal-arising, I would never say there is a true, final escape from the born, the arisen, the made, the conditioned, and the equal-arising. Because there truly is the unborn, the unarisen, the unmade, the unconditioned, and the unequal-arising, I therefore say there is a true, final escape from the born, the arisen, the made, the conditioned, and the equal-arising.

items.title: Section: Profound, Vast, Immeasurable, Beyond Reckoning — Neither Form Nor Apart From Form, Neither Feeling Nor Apart From Feeling

items.zh: 世尊依此密意說言甚深、廣大、無量、無數，是謂寂滅。由於此中所具功德難了知故，名為甚深。極寬博故，名為廣大。無窮盡故，名為無量。數不能數，無二說故，名為無數。云何此中數不能數？謂有非有不可說故，即色離色不可說故，即受離受不可說故，即想離想不可說故，即行離行不可說故，即識離識不可說故。所以者何？由此清淨真如所顯，一向無垢，是名無損惱寂滅。如是二種，總說為一寂滅施設安立。
items.en:
Third, revealing the meaning; first, naming cessation. The Blessed One, with this hidden intention, says it is profound, vast, immeasurable, and beyond reckoning; this too is called cessation.
Second, explaining the scriptural names; first, profound. Because the qualities contained herein are difficult to understand, it is called profound.
Second, vast. Because it is extremely broad, it is called vast.
Third, immeasurable. Because it is inexhaustible, it is called immeasurable.
Fourth, beyond reckoning; first, stating overall. Because it cannot be reckoned through discrimination, admitting no second way of speaking of it, it is called beyond reckoning.
Second, explaining individually. Why can it not be reckoned here? Because existence and non-existence alike cannot be said of it; because it cannot be said identical to form, nor apart from form; likewise for feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Third, revealing the meaning. Why is this so? Because what this pure suchness reveals is, without exception, free of defilement.
Third, concluding. This is called cessation through freedom from affliction.
Fifth, concluding. These two kinds together are jointly called the single establishment of cessation.

items.title: Section: Twenty-Five Names for Nirvāṇa — Home, Island, Refuge, Ambrosia, and the Final Word Itself

items.zh: 云何寂滅異門施設安立？當知此中，寂滅異門有無量種。謂名為常，亦名為恒，亦名久住，亦名無變，亦名有法，亦名舍宅，亦名洲渚，亦名救護，亦名歸依，亦名所趣，亦名安隱，亦名淡泊，亦名善事，亦名吉祥，亦名無轉，亦名無垢，亦名難見，亦名甘露，亦名無憂，亦名無沒，亦名無熾，亦名無熱，亦名無病，亦名無動，亦名涅槃，
items.en:
Third, the establishment of synonyms for cessation; first, posing the question. What is the establishment of synonyms for cessation?
Second, stating. Know that the synonyms for cessation are innumerable in kind.
Third, listing them; first, listing individually. It is called permanent, also called eternal, also called long-abiding, also called unchanging, also called existent, also called home, also called an island, also called rescue, also called refuge, also called destination, also called peace, also called tranquil, also called a virtuous matter, also called auspicious, also called unturning, also called stainless, also called hard to see, also called ambrosia, also called sorrowless, also called unsubmerged, also called unblazing, also called feverless, also called unmoving, also called nirvāṇa.

items.title: Section: Why Each Name Fits, "The Permanent Severance of All Proliferation" — and the Seventeen Stages Reach Their End

items.zh: 亦名永絕一切戲論。如是等類，應知說名寂滅異門。是名寂滅異門施設安立。
items.en:
Also called the permanent severance of all conceptual proliferation.
Commentary: as for this final name — this means that whether it is different or not different from the aggregates, whether something exists or fails to exist after death, and every such proliferating discourse, cannot be said of it at all.
Second, briefly gathering them together. All such kinds as these should be understood as called the synonyms for cessation.
Fourth, concluding. This is called the establishment of synonyms for cessation.

blocks.text: A landmark day. The seventeenth stage, "without remainder" (無餘依地), ends the first great division of the treatise, the "Basic Section" (本地分) on the seventeen stages, begun on Day 1.

The first is the five aggregates of clinging. Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging is affliction; through it these aggregates are obtained. Venerable Miào Jìng: without names we cannot think, and without notions we cannot speak.
Edible, contact, volitional, and consciousness food. Master Cháng Bǎi: contact includes watching plays or scenery; the first three strengthen consciousness.
Both lecturers: these four stations are where consciousness rests and grows.
Venerable Miào Jìng: demons leave desire-realm goodness alone; their target is one seeking to leave desire.
"The reliance of the final limit." Venerable Miào Jìng: without afflictions, the aggregates still remain; arhats too must eat and meet displeasure. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily pain without mental pain.

Master Cháng Bǎi: entering nirvāṇa without remainder, the arhat has four supreme tranquillities. Venerable Miào Jìng: the practitioner asks, "Will there be suffering in nirvāṇa without remainder?" Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people assume arhats still suffer as they do.

Both lecturers: "birth" is the first moment, "arising" its continuation. Master Cháng Bǎi: the passage shows that people have truly entered nirvāṇa without remainder; it is not a logical deduction. Venerable Miào Jìng: even if you cannot yet, you are told it is so.

"Profound … vast … immeasurable": its qualities are hard to understand. Master Cháng Bǎi: suchness is neither identical to nor apart from the aggregates. Venerable Miào Jìng: beyond all marks, yet it manifests aggregates to save beings.
Home, island, refuge, ambrosia, and more. (Ru-Yi drops 無病, "without sickness"; Venerable Miào Jìng: it means without the sickness of affliction.)

Fifty fascicles and four hundred and fifty-four days: from the five consciousnesses on Day 1 to the twenty-five names of nirvāṇa today. The treatise now turns to its second division, which explains the difficult points of the seventeen stages.

quiz.q: What is relied upon in the reliance of designation?
quiz.why: The five aggregates of clinging. Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging is affliction; through it these aggregates are obtained.

quiz.q: "Every such notion, and equivalent notion." How does Venerable Miào Jìng take 等想?
options: all sorts of differing notions; without notions one cannot speak
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: all kinds of differing notions; without names we can't think, and without notions we can't speak. "Equivalent" misses this.

quiz.q: What are the four foods of sustenance?
quiz.why: Edible, contact, volitional, and consciousness food. Master Cháng Bǎi: contact includes watching plays or scenery; the first three strengthen consciousness.

quiz.q: Why are the four stations form, feeling, perception, and formations, not consciousness?
options: they are where consciousness rests, grows, and expands
quiz.why: Both: these four are where consciousness rests and grows.

quiz.q: The English says demons obstruct "wherever wholesome dharma is being cultivated." What does Venerable Miào Jìng add?
options: they leave desire-realm good alone; they come when one seeks to leave desire
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: demons leave desire-realm goodness alone; the target is one seeking to leave desire. Master Cháng Bǎi: mainly demons of the Paranirmita heaven.

quiz.q: To which reliance does the arhat fully and exclusively correspond?
quiz.why: The reliance of the final limit. Venerable Miào Jìng: without afflictions, the aggregates still remain.

quiz.q: "Does not correspond to six matters of care." What remains, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: corresponding with the sixth, meritorious and skilful work; the other six do not
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from the sixth, meritorious and skilful work, the other six do not correspond.

quiz.q: "With the remaining reliances, neither." What examples do the lectures give?
options: he eats and meets displeasure, but the mind suffers not, unbound
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: arhats too must eat and meet displeasure. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodily pain without mental pain; the mind isn't bound.

quiz.q: The English says "these same four most excellent kinds." Is that right?
options: no: the two sets of four differ
quiz.why: The two lists differ, so "same four" is inexact. Master Cháng Bǎi: entering no-residue nirvāṇa, the arhat has four supreme tranquilities.

quiz.q: In "tranquility from doubt arising from the reliance's suffering," whose doubt is it?
options: they differ: Miào Jìng: the practitioner's own doubt about future suffering; Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people doubting arhats who eat and get sick
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the practitioner asks, "Will there be suffering in no-residue nirvāṇa?" Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people assume arhats still suffer as they do.

quiz.q: "Equal-arising" renders 等生起. How do the lectures explain 生, 起, and 等生起?
options: first moment is birth, continuing is arising; Cháng Bǎi: 等 means complete, the body fully formed
quiz.why: Both: the first moment is birth, continuing is arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: 等 means complete. "Equal-arising" is merely literal.

quiz.q: The English note reads this as a logical necessity. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: it's that people have truly succeeded; Miào Jìng: though you can't yet do it, you're told it exists
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it proves that people have truly succeeded in entering no-residue nirvāṇa, not a logical deduction. Venerable Miào Jìng: even if you cannot yet, you are told it is so.

options: its qualities are hard to understand
quiz.why: Because its qualities are hard to understand. Vast is broad; immeasurable is inexhaustible.

quiz.q: "Cannot be said identical to form, nor apart from form." How do the lectures explain?
options: suchness and aggregates are neither one nor other; Miào Jìng: beyond all marks yet manifesting aggregates to save beings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: suchness is neither identical to nor apart from the aggregates. Venerable Miào Jìng: beyond all marks, yet it manifests aggregates to save beings.

quiz.q: How does the English list of synonyms differ from the treatise, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng add?
options: the English omits "無病"; Miào Jìng: it means no sickness of affliction
quiz.why: After "unblazing, feverless," the English goes directly to "unmoving," dropping 無病. Venerable Miào Jìng: it means no sickness of affliction.
